text:
maria_support: FYI — Customer (Acme Health) opened an escalation: API responses after a failover are mangled (weird tokens, truncated JSON). They say it started when their requests were routed to another region.
kevin_infra: can you drop the request_id and sample response? I want to grep the routing logs
maria_support: request_id=req_01H8Z7K4. Example request (sanitized):

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx" \ 
  -H "X-Region: eu-west-1" \ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-bison-v1","input":"Summarize patient intake form"}'
```
response snippet:
```
{"id":"resp_9abc","text":"Ġ<|role|>patient\n\nĠ<|content|>Name: John Doe\n<|pad|> ..."}
```
maria_support: customer says sometimes they get eloquent answer, then suddenly outputs with raw token markers and broken JSON — happens during higher traffic periods.
deploy-bot: traffic-policy service rolled out config `allow_cross_region_fallback=true` in rollout `routing-2026-02-14` (commit 8e3b2d4) at 2026-02-14T03:12Z
emily_sre: :eyes: that rollout could explain cross-region fallbacks. Did we validate model-variant compatibility mapping with that change?
luca_eng: Noticed that routing fallback currently picks any "compatible_architecture" variant, but we don't check tokenizer/version metadata. That can cause fallback to quantized/legacy variants with different tokenizers.
kevin_infra: grepping logs for req_01H8Z7K4 shows:
```
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] req=req_01H8Z7K4 route=euw1 -> fallback=usw2 variant=rwd-bison-quant8
[2026-03-09T14:22:11Z] tokenizer_mismatch=true token_scheme=bytepair expected=cl100k_base got=cl100k_legacy
```
kevin_infra: so the router fell back to `rwd-bison-quant8` in us-west and that variant uses an older tokenizer (cl100k_legacy) — mismatch flagged in logs.
maria_support: customer pasted one of the broken outputs, includes literal `<|pad|>` and some control bytes that break their JSON parser. They flagged as high severity.
luca_eng: immediate mitigation options:
- revert `allow_cross_region_fallback` rollout (prevents cross-region fallback while we patch)
- blacklist specific variants from fallback unless tokenizer_version matches
- update routing preflight to validate tokenizer metadata before sending
emily_sre: revert first please, we need to stop new incidents. I'll coordinate oncall to approve.
maria_support: customer wants ETA and escalation to CSM — any estimate if we can stop this within the hour?
luca_eng: if infra agrees, we can rollback the rollout in ~10-15m. For long term we need a small router change (~2h dev + 30m deploy) to enforce tokenizer compatibility in fallback selection.
kevin_infra: rolling back now. running: `trafficctl rollback routing-2026-02-14` — will post updates in 5.
deploy-bot: rollback of `routing-2026-02-14` started by kevin_infra at 2026-03-09T14:29Z
emily_sre: good. After rollback, please run a targeted replay for the request id and confirm outputs stable.
kevin_infra: replayed req_01H8Z7K4 against euw1 primary -> response clean, no tokenizer markers. replayed forced fallback -> response had markers. Logs updated.
luca_eng: I'll open a small PR to add tokenizer_version checks to the fallback matcher and add a unit test that simulates different tokenizers (PR: rrdw/routing#452). ETA 2 hours for patch and staging test, then can canary to 5%.
maria_support: please include sample text we can send CSM to explain cause/mitigation. Customer asked for reason: why did requests go to us-west and why variant changed?
luca_eng: suggested message:
"We traced this to a recently enabled cross-region fallback policy; the router selected a lower-latency fallback variant in another region that had an incompatible tokenizer. This caused token markers and malformed JSON in some responses. We rolled back the policy to stop new incidents and are patching the router to validate tokenizer/version compatibility before fallback."
maria_support: perfect. tagging CSM.
emily_sre: action items:
- kevin_infra: confirm rollback fully rolled out (in progress)
- luca_eng: PR for tokenizer check + tests
- maria_support: update customer and log incident ticket
- ops: monitor spike in cross-region traffic
maria_support: updating ticket INC-2026-318 and CSM. will keep thread updated. thanks team :heart:
luca_eng: once PR merged will create a short runbook snippet: "if cross-region fallback is enabled, ensure `tokenizer_version` in model metadata matches before routing" — will attach to incident.
kevin_infra: rollback completed at 2026-03-09T14:36Z. monitoring for reruns.
emily_sre: :thumbsup: closing escalation until we see reoccurrence. maria, please post if customer still sees issues.
